blocks.text: Managing your inbox as an estate planner

Estate planners deal with sensitive documents and urgent client requests. Your inbox is often the first place these arrive. Start by organizing your folder structure to mirror your client files. Use the Outlook sidebar to create subfolders for each active matter. You can create a folder in Outlook by right-clicking your Inbox and selecting New Folder. Do this for each client to keep correspondence separated from general administrative noise.

Efficiency on a Mac comes from keeping your hands on the keyboard. Use ⌘ + 1 to jump to Mail. Use ⌘ + 2 for your Calendar. Use ⌘ + 3 to view your Contacts. If you need to start a new message, press ⌘ + N. Sending a completed email is as simple as pressing ⌘ + Return. These shortcuts save seconds that add up to minutes over the course of a long day.
If a shortcut does not work, check your System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts. You can manually map menu commands here if they conflict with other Mac apps.
blocks.title: Fixing Shortcut Conflicts

blocks.text: You likely receive many emails with the same subject lines or from the same firms. Instead of moving these manually, set up rules. Go to Tools > Rules to define conditions. You can move emails with specific keywords into a folder automatically. This ensures your primary inbox only contains items requiring your immediate attention. It is a simple way to reduce the time you spend on manual sorting.
Working with the New Outlook for Mac

Microsoft has moved to the New Outlook for Mac interface. This version is built for modern cloud services. If you are still using the Legacy version, be aware that support for Exchange Web Services is ending in October 2026. Transitioning early allows you to learn the new layout. The search bar is now more powerful, allowing for complex filters. You can use search with filters in Outlook to find specific client documents by date, sender, or attachment type.

Drafting repetitive emails takes time you could spend on billable work. Create an email signature in Outlook that includes your contact details and a link to your booking calendar. This reduces the back and forth needed to schedule meetings. If you find yourself typing the same instructions for clients, use templates or a text expansion tool. Keep your responses concise to lower the chance of long, unmanageable threads.
Using Lazur in your daily practice

Lazur works as a voice assistant that lives in your Mac notch. When you are overwhelmed by email, hold the fn key to dictate your replies. It formats your text at the cursor in Outlook. If you are lost in a menu, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where a setting is. It will circle the button on your screen. This keeps your focus on your legal work rather than hunting for interface items.

Scheduling meetings with clients and other counsel is a major part of your day. Use the Outlook calendar to manage these appointments. When you send a meeting invite, include a clear agenda and any documents they need to review beforehand. This prepares the client and makes the meeting more productive. You can change your default calendar in Outlook if you manage multiple accounts.

faq.question: Is Outlook for Mac fully compatible with my firm's Exchange server?
faq.answer: Yes, but you must use the New Outlook for Mac interface. Legacy support is being phased out through October 2026.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Outlook's email editor?
faq.answer: Yes. You can hold the fn key to dictate your email text directly into the body of your message in Outlook.

faq.question: Can I use custom keyboard shortcuts in Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, you can add them through System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts on your Mac.

faq.question: How do I find where a setting moved in the new Outlook?
faq.answer: Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where the setting is. It will point to the location on your screen.
